findings.title: Shard-split path keeps targets whose expression interpolates to empty, so `runSplitGroupedQueries` throws on an empty request list and the query never emits
findings.description: Before this diff, `runShardSplitQuery` interpolated first and then filtered on `query.expr`, so a target such as `$query` with an empty value was dropped. The diff moves the `expr` filter ahead of the `.map(applyTemplateVariables)` (lines 50 and 52), so an empty expression is only produced after the filter and nothing removes it. The target goes through `groupTargetsByQueryType` (lines 238-279). If it ends up alone in its group, `runNextRequest` calls `runSplitQuery` on it (line 163). That function filters `query.expr` again (querySplitting.ts:298), which leaves `requests` empty. `runSplitGroupedQueries` then evaluates `requests.filter(...)[0].partition` (querySplitting.ts:96), which throws a TypeError. The throw happens inside the `.then` callback at shardQuerySplitting.ts:213-215, which has no catch, so the observable never calls `next` or `complete` and the panel stays in a loading state. The trigger is a request that also contains a shard-eligible target, which is what routes it to this path (datasource.ts:336). The path is gated by the experimental `lokiShardSplitting` toggle (pkg/services/featuremgmt/registry.go:151-155).

findings.title: Split paths apply template variables twice, so an ad hoc value containing `$name` is replaced with the matching dashboard variable's value
findings.description: `runSplitQuery` now calls `applyTemplateVariables` (line 299). That method runs `templateSrv.replace` on the expression and then `addAdHocFilters` (datasource.ts:1127-1130), which inserts the ad hoc value verbatim. `escapeLabelValueInExactSelector` (languageUtils.ts:38-40) does not escape `$`. The expression then reaches `datasource.runQuery(subRequest)` (querySplitting.ts:180), then `super.query`, and `DataSourceWithBackend.query` calls `this.applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` a second time (DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185). That second `templateSrv.replace` scans the whole string, including the inserted value. A filter value such as `cost $region` therefore becomes `cost us-east-1` when a dashboard variable named `region` exists. Before this diff, the split path interpolated once, after the ad hoc insertion, so the literal value was sent. The shard path adds a third pass (shardQuerySplitting.ts:52). The updated test expects `applyTemplateVariables` to be called 5 times for a single target (shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112), which is consistent with the repeated passes. The trigger needs `$name` text in an ad hoc value or variable value that matches a variable name. The path is reachable by default: `lokiQuerySplitting` is GA (registry.go:158-161) and datasource.ts:338-339 sends any request with a non-empty expression through `runSplitQuery`.
